# f5xc_service_policy (Data Source)

ServicePolicy data source

The `f5xc_service_policy` data source allows you to retrieve information about an existing configuration within your F5 XC tenant.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "f5xc_service_policy" "example" {
  name      = "example_service_policy"
  namespace = "example_namespace"
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `name` (String) name This is the name of configuration object. It has to be unique within the namespace. It can only be specified during create API and cannot be changed during replace API. The value of name has to follow DNS-1035 format.
- `namespace` (String) namespace This defines the workspace within which each the configuration object is to be created. Must be a DNS_LABEL format. For a namespace object itself, namespace value will be ''
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `annotations` (Map of String) annotations Annotations is an unstructured key value map stored with a resource that may be set by external tools to store and retrieve arbitrary metadata. They are not queryable and should be preserved when modifying objects.

- `rule_choice` (Attributes) rule choice Allowed/Denied Sources rules provide the ability to allow/deny lists of IP addresses, countries, TLS fingerprints and ASNs. Custom rules provide more flexibility to define your own logic to control incoming requests. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rule_choice))
- `server_choice` (Attributes) server choice Select servers for which the policy will be applied. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--server_choice))
- `uid` (String) uid uid is the unique in time and space value for this object. Object create will fail if provided by the client and the value exists in the system. Typically generated by the server on successful creation of an object and is not allowed to change once populated. Shadowed by SystemObjectMeta's uid field.

<a id="nestedatt--server_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `server_choice`

Read-Only:

- `any_server` (Boolean) any Any Server
- `server_name` (String) server name The expected name of the server to which the request API is directed. The actual names for the server are extracted from the HTTP Host header and the name of the virtual_host to which the request is directed. If the request is directed to a virtual K8s service, the actual names also contain the name of that service. The predicate evaluates to true if any of the actual names is the same as the expected server name.
- `server_name_matcher` (Attributes) server name matcher A list of exact values and/or regular expressions for the expected name of the server. The actual names of server are extracted from the HTTP Host header and the name of the virtual_host to which the request is directed. If the request is directed to a virtual K8s service, the actual names also contain the name of that service. This is a generalized version of the server name predicate that allows the same rule to be applicable to a set of server rather than a single server. The predicate evaluates to true if any of the server's actual names match any of the exact values or regular expressions in the server name matcher. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--server_choice--server_name_matcher))
- `server_selector` (Attributes) server selector A label selector that describes the expected set of servers. The labels associated with the server to which the API request is directed are used to evaluate the label expressions in the selector. These labels are derived from the server TLS certificate and the virtual host object for the server. If the request is directed to a virtual K8s service, the K8s labels for the service are also included in the set of server labels. This is a more flexible and powerful version of the server name matcher predicate that allows a given policy to be applicable to a set of servers based on the server labels rather than being limited to relying on patterns in the server name. The predicate evaluates to true if the expressions in the label selector are true for the server labels. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--server_choice--server_selector))

<a id="nestedatt--server_choice--server_name_matcher"></a>
### Nested Schema for `server_choice.server_name_matcher`

- `regex_values` (List of String) regex values A list of regular expressions to match the input against.
